newsitem.title: CHINA: SHENZHEN B INDEX SOARS TO CLOSE AT LIMIT-UP.
newsitem.headline: SHENZHEN B INDEX SOARS TO CLOSE AT LIMIT-UP.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index held to its upper limit at Thursday's close, fuelled by a heavy diversion of funds from the more expensive Hong Kong market and on rumours of an easing of trading curbs, analysts said.
The hard currency index leapt 13.78 points to its 10 percent limit-up level of 151.22 while turnover more than doubled to HK$266 million from Wednesday's HK$103 million.
"This is a historic moment for the B share market when just about every issue hit its limit-up level," said Cheng Li, an analyst at China Guotai Securities.
The domestic currency A share index followed suit but with less gusto, rising 11.15 points, or 3.01 percent, to 382.01 on turnover of 3.4 billion yuan, compared with 3.2 billion on Wednesday.
"Today's strong B share performance was brought on by the widening price differential between Shenzhen's B shares and Hong Kong's H shares," an analyst at J&A Securities said.

China's B shares have shed about 30 percent in the three months since Beijing clamped down in mid-May to end on what it saw as excessive stock speculation, while share prices in Hong Kong have been charging higher.
Recent sharp gains in Hong Kong's mainland shares, or H shares, saw some investors cashing in and shifting positions to relatively cheap B shares, brokers said.

Rumours were also swirling in the market that Beijing may allow Sino-foreign investment funds, through which domestic investors could buy B shares. These hard currency shares are officially limited only to foreign investors.
A senior official at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange said he had received no notice of such a move, and denied that the Thursday's sharp rise was linked to possible policy changes.
Although the B shares ended mainly up at their 10 percent ceiling imposed by the government to narrow price movements, some recently-listed stocks shone on heavy trading volumes.

The heavily capitalised Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd was the most actively traded stock with 24.4 million shares changing hands. Its shares, which closed at HK$2.59, shot through the HK$2.38 issue price.
Another newcomer, Beijing Orient Electronics (Group) Co Ltd, jumped HK$0.41 to HK$4.50 on volume of 3.7 million shares.
